newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares shake off slump to set new record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares shake off slump to set new record.

text.p: Swiss shares overcame midday weakness to end with minor gains that set a record for the second day in a row.

Dealers said short-covering revived the afternoon market after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) had slumped below the crucial level of 3,800 points at midday on profit taking, an easier dollar and lower government bonds futures.
The SMI ended up 0.12 percent, or 4.4 points, at 3,818.1. The prior record was set on Monday at 3,813.7, narrowly beating the high mark set in July.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 2.86 points, or 0.12 percent, to 2,442.85 points. Most shares posted gains towards the end of the session, a trader noted.
Heavily-traded CS Holding advanced 1.75 Swiss francs to 129.75 and industrial group Elektrowatt added 19 francs to 509.
Renewed speculation that CS Holding intended to sell its 45 percent stake in Elektrowatt influenced the market again, a dealer said.

Some investors hoped for news of a possible spin-off to emerge from CS Holding's extraordinary shareholders' meeting on Friday. The meeting has been set to change the name of CS Holding to Credit Suisse Group.
In other sectors, Nestle lost six francs to 1,403. Among financials, insurer Winterthur and UBS were weaker.
Watch company TAG Heuer fell 14.25 francs to 227.25. Second-tier Maag jumped 35 percent on Monday's news the group was selling part of its industrial business to Sinter Metals.
